title: Six tons of missing fissionable material at Chernobyl

tellings.quote: >> Six tons of fisionable material that was at the plant, not in the reactors. Was it was at the plant was missing.

plain: After the 1986 disaster at Chernobyl, a nuclear power plant in the Soviet Union, six tons of fissionable material, the kind of nuclear fuel that can sustain a chain reaction, went missing from the plant. A former Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan tells this to Jesse Michels and stresses that the material was stored at the plant, not inside the reactors. If true, it would mean a large amount of nuclear material was unaccounted for.
